### Final reviewed graph answer

Sound as a proposed protocol, not demonstrated feasibility.

Pair fixed-original versus movable wrists on all 258 inputs; freeze anatomy, geometry, contacts, initialization, objective and budget. Re-audit originals identically. Only wrist freedom changes.

Independently audit every output:
- Complete surface-vertex clearance and no triangle/solid interior intersection at **0.01 mm tolerance**, both quad diagonals.
- Retained actual on-key skin anchors within **0.1 mm** of rotating tops.
- Unchanged joint limits; neighboring joint speeds **≤12 rad/s** and wrist speeds **≤0.8 m/s**, using original timestamps.
- Exact two-bone lengths/reachability and proxy spacing.

Speeds are engineering bounds, not physiology.

Report per-probe paired pass/fail transitions, regressions, penetration, anchor errors, every missed score contact, and solver status separately. Restoration improvement requires increased fully accepted outputs versus originals; wrist advantage requires improvement over fixed wrists. Failed checks remain failures regardless of optimizer status. Note deletion or anatomy changes invalidate comparison.

Supplied IPC excerpts—not independent full-paper verification—describe intersection-free starts, positive primitive distances, linear nodal trajectories, and barrier/Newton with filtered CCD. Penetrating-start SLSQP inherits no guarantees.

Next: continuous collision gates for nonlinear articulation, then coupled trajectory/body solving. Exact self/interhand/body/cloth safety and elbow timing remain unestablished. Static acceptance establishes neither playable performance nor force-based simulation.

**VERDICT: PASS** — review of the proposed protocol, not an empirical experiment result.
